Orchot Tzadikim 28:11: Therefore you must be informed of the matter of the soul, its power and its might, so that you may set your mind upon the supernal foundation. This matter is comparable to a king's son, a child of one or two years old, who was stolen away and carried a thousand parasangs or more, and was raised in the house of a peasant, and was trained in peasant ways, and never thought of nor remembered his royal lineage, for he neither recognized nor knew it. And after he came to his senses, someone came to him and gave him the news, saying, "You are a king's son!" But he did not tell him whose son he was. Then his heart was lifted somewhat, but he was not greatly moved, since he did not know who his father was. Afterward another messenger came to him and told him which king was his father, and told him his kingdom and his land. Then his heart was lifted still more, and he longed to go there. Nevertheless his heart sank when he remembered, "Even if I go there, they will pay me no heed, for they do not know me!" Afterward the king heard where his son was, and sent after him members of his own household who recognized the marks on his body, and sent with them nobles and royal garments to bring his son to him. And when these came to him and saw him and recognized him, and showed him the royal garments — then his heart was lifted greatly. And after they had dressed him and mounted him on the horse the king himself rode — then he knew his own strength and might, and he had the heart of a king, and was lifted up very, very high. So it is with the matter of the soul: she is a king's daughter, breathed into man from the Throne of Glory, and brought into a soiled body whose desire for this world is very great and which has all manner of appetites, until the soul, though she is the king's daughter, becomes fixed among them and is drawn after the desires of the body and forgets her Father above. But when the heavens are shown to her, and the stars, and the sun, and the moon, and how they conduct themselves in a fixed and constant order, and she is told that she was created by the One who created them — then she rises higher and higher. And when she is taught the secret of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the secret of the wisdom of the soul — then she puts on royal garments and enters into the secret of the fear of Heaven. And even a person who knows none of this, when he reflects deeply from the depth of his heart, and discerns the mighty acts of God, blessed be He — then awe will clothe his heart, as it is written (Isaiah 40:26): "Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name; by the greatness of His might, and for that He is strong in power, not one is missing."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:12: And the Holy One, blessed be He, gave permission to no nation in the world to declare His praise except Israel, as it is said (Isaiah 43:21): "This people I have formed for Myself, they shall declare My praise." And it is written (Deuteronomy 7:6): "For you are a holy people to the Lord your God." And it is written (Deuteronomy 26:18): "And the Lord has avouched you this day to be His treasured people." And it is written (Deuteronomy 26:19): "And to set you high above all nations." And likewise the Holy One, blessed be He, gave no creature the knowledge of the blessed Name except Israel, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:35): "To you it was shown, that you might know that the Lord is God; there is none else beside Him." And it is written (Deuteronomy 4:8): "And what great nation is there that has statutes and judgments so righteous as all this law?" And it is written (Deuteronomy 6:13): "You shall fear the Lord your God, and Him shall you serve."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:13: And from these verses we learn that Israel is obligated to fear the blessed Name, and to occupy itself with the study of His Torah and to fulfill His commandments — for out of the fear of the Lord, may He be exalted, they will engage in Torah and fulfill His commandments, and out of the study of the Torah they will understand the explanations of its reasons and its novel insights, and will grow wise to know the blessed Name, and His power and His might and His greatness, and His great, awesome, and wondrous works, as it is written (Psalms 66:3): "Say to God, how awesome are Your works!" And it is written (Psalms 34:12): "Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the Lord."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:14: There is nothing in the world equal in weight to the fear of Heaven — not silver, not gold, not pearls, and not all treasures; all of them are as nothing next to the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, for "the fear of the Lord, that is His treasure" (Isaiah 33:6). Therefore let a person hasten to store away in the treasury of his heart the thing that is the treasure of the Holy One, blessed be He. And let a person learn from this world, that every person strives to store away as much good as he is able, and whoever is able to store it away like kings certainly does so. If so, who would not store away that which the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself stores away?
Orchot Tzadikim 28:15: And now I will inform you of the wisdom of the nefesh, the ruach, and the neshamah, in order that you may fear the Holy One, blessed be He. The nefesh is the liver, for the blood is the nefesh. It desires to eat and to drink, and craves dominion and its own gratification, for the liver is full of blood and craves delicacies and pleasures; and this is the meaning of (Proverbs 27:7): "A sated soul (nefesh) tramples honeycomb." The ruach is the heart, and it seeks rulership, greatness, and dominion in the hearts of men, pursuing honor. Therefore the pride of the heart is called "haughtiness of ruach." It is this that lifts up the mind of men to seek rule and greatness. The neshamah is wisdom, and it sits in the brain like a king among his troops, and resembles the honor of its Creator, and it despises the pleasures of men and the vanities of their delights. It makes wise and gives understanding, and all its thoughts are to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, in fear, and it considers what will be in the end, when the body dies and perishes, and how it will return in purity to the One who created it and placed it within the body.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:16: A person has two masters, and at his death he becomes free of them, as it is said (Job 3:19): "The small and the great are there, and the servant is free from his master." The two masters are the ruach and the nefesh, which think of pleasures, and of increasing wealth, and of eating and drinking, and of rejoicing, and of doing all that the heart devises and the eyes behold, and of speaking vain words and gratifying the body. But the neshamah overturns their thoughts and says: "What worth has a man, and what profit has he from all his labor that he labors, seeing that in a single moment he is no more, and the body perishes — where then is his wisdom and his beauty? If so, there is no good but to serve the Holy One, blessed be He, and to cling to Him."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:17: This one says one thing and that one says another. If the nefesh and the ruach prevail, then the neshamah is weakened and has no power to stand against them. Therefore one who occupies himself with eating and drinking will never grow wise. But when the neshamah prevails over the ruach and the nefesh, then the eyes of the neshamah are opened to understand the wisdom of the supernal realms. Therefore the neshamah must weaken the ruach, from which anger and pride issue, and the nefesh, which is the possessor of desire. And when the neshamah prevails through wisdom, it brings a person to humility.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:18: The beast, too, has a nefesh and a ruach, for the beast desires and grows angry just as man does. But man alone has an additional neshamah, which speaks and which distinguishes between truth and falsehood. And when the body dies, the nefesh of desire and the nefesh of ruach die, and the form of the supernal, wise neshamah remains, for it does not die with the death of the body, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 12:7): "And the ruach shall return to God who gave it" — this is the ruach of wisdom. But when a person sins, the soul-life of his nefesh and the soul-life of his ruach die, as it is written (Ezekiel 18:4): "The soul (nefesh) that sins, it shall die." And Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, the man of God, said (Leviticus 23:30): "And I will destroy that soul (nefesh) from among its people" — learn from this that it calls "nefesh" the part of a person that dies. And after the death of the wicked man, the wise neshamah slings him away as with a sling's pouch, because it listened to the ruach and the nefesh. But the nefesh of the righteous man, in whom the supernal neshamah prevailed over the ruach and the nefesh, is bound up beneath the Throne of Glory. And the fool who listened to the ruach and the nefesh — his neshamah shall surely be cut off. And the wise man who listened to the supernal neshamah, which was breathed into him from the Throne of Glory — his neshamah shall merit abundant good that is stored away.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:19: And now incline your ear, and understand and know that the neshamah dwells in the heart, and it is the seat of the fear of Heaven, for from there come forth the products of thought. And thought rises and swells within the chambers of the heart, as the waves of the sea rise up. The neshamah inquires and investigates and reflects upon all deeds, and the heart roams in its wisdom to distant places and beholds in its vision many matters; in a single brief moment it calculates this way and that, and runs and returns from one matter to another. The Rock of the ages made man wise and gave him understanding, and taught him wisdom and knowledge.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:20: And by this wisdom man remembers all that has passed and foresees all that will come to be. And by this wisdom he makes wheels and millstones to grind without toil. And by this wisdom he raises armies and musters soldiers and marshals them, and succeeds in his kingship, and governs his dominion and holds it firm. And by this wisdom he spreads nets into the deep recesses of the seas and rivers, to catch fish from the depths of the abyss. And by this wisdom he hunts the beasts of the wilderness, and by it he traps the birds that fly in the heights of the heavens. And by it he knows and understands the ailments of the body and their remedies, seeking out cures, and discerns the benefit and the harm of drugs, and recognizes roots and herbs and the varieties of fruits — the cold and the hot, the moist and the dry. And by it he knows how to give the body to drink of medicinal potions, to restore it to its proper strength.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:21: And behold, your own eyes see the greatness of man and his honor, for the Holy One, blessed be He, made him great and exalted him above all creatures, and gave him dominion over all the creatures below, and there is no power in any mouth to recount the multitude of works that man performs in the lower world. And even in the upper world man sends forth his desire, and flies and soars on the wings of wisdom. Although his body walks upon the earth like the beasts and the creeping things, his neshamah walks in the upper world because of its abundant wisdom, and it contemplates and knows the science of the supernal realms, and the science of the heavens, and the course of the stars and the measure of their stature. Although a man's body is very small, his neshamah is greater and broader than the heavens and the earth, for it knows their height and their loftiness, and the paths of the sun and the constellations and all their divisions — all of it enters into the neshamah. And since everything is contained within it, it must therefore be greater than all of them; for were this not so, it would not be able to contain it all, since it is impossible to pour the waters of the sea into a small flask.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:22: Now, seeing that man rules by his wisdom over two worlds, the lower world and the upper world, it is fitting for every person to consider and reflect: why did the Holy One, blessed be He, make all this known to him? It was for no other purpose than that he should be wise enough to serve Him with a whole heart, for when a person understands and recognizes these great and awesome wonders, it is fitting for him to humble himself and to subjugate the body to the neshamah. For all these great forms of wisdom belong to the neshamah and not to the body, for the neshamah governs the body, as a man rides upon a horse and directs it and turns it wherever he wishes; thus the horse is subordinate to the man, and the man is not subordinate to the horse. Therefore woe, alas, and grief to those who subjugate the neshamah to the body, and cast down the essential thing beneath the hand of that which is subordinate to it.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:23: And this too may be known: since the upper world serves the lower world — the sun, the moon, and the stars — it is certain and clear that this is not for the benefit of the body, that it should enjoy the pleasure of this world; for there is no substance in it, and it is dust, a worm, and a maggot, ready for mishaps and prepared for death. And the sun, the moon, and the stars are pure and clear — how could it be that so great a matter should serve the perishing, decaying body? Rather, it is the neshamah, which is clear and pure, and is raised up above the heavens and higher than them, and is greater than the heavens and the earth, for the knowledge of heaven and earth enters into it and it encompasses them — this, in truth, is a great argument and proof that the heavens and the earth were created for the sake of the neshamah and to serve it.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:24: And let it reflect and consider: "Who am I, that the heavens and the earth were created for my sake? It is for no other purpose than that I should subjugate myself to the Holy One, blessed be He, to understand His wonders and to praise Him and glorify Him!" And were it not for the Torah, in order to refine and purify the soul of man, what need would he have of the world at all? And is it a reasonable thought that the world was created for the benefit of the body, for darkness and lowliness?
Orchot Tzadikim 28:25: Now, seeing that man was chosen above all creatures because of his abundant wisdom and his abundant deeds — for all creatures are subjugated to man, and he has within him the power to learn wisdom and to understand deep secrets, the mysteries of the lower and upper worlds — this is a clear sign to a man that his soul shall be bound up in the bond of life, if he keeps the Torah. To what may this be compared? To a king who brought his servants into his innermost chambers and showed them his treasures and pearls and all his stores, and gave them dominion and rule over all of this, and revealed to them his secrets, and warned them to remain faithful to him, and then he would grant them great good and raise them up doubly, many times more than they had been until now. And this shall be a sign to them: that he revealed to them his secrets and his treasures, and gave them true dominion over his land — by this they shall discern that the king speaks the truth. So too the Holy One, blessed be He, showed man His greatness and His splendor, and revealed to him His secrets of the upper and lower worlds, and gave him dominion over all — certainly by this he shall discern the abundance of his greatness in the time to come, if he is careful in the service of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:26: There is also great proof that the neshamah comes from above: for we see that no person is ever satisfied with what he has, but forever seeks a higher rank than his own. If he has a thousand, he covets two thousand; if he is a minister in this province, he seeks to be ruler of another province; and you will not find a king or a minister who does not seek a higher rank than his own. And this comes about because the neshamah does not attach itself to these material goods, but ever desires greater and higher attainments, for it is higher than all created things. And therefore man walks upright because of the neshamah, while the rest of creation walks upon its belly and bent over.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:27: And because the neshamah comes from above, from the Throne of Glory, therefore the body in which it dwells contains within it a likeness of the whole world, and therefore man is called a "small world." The neshamah is like its Creator, and the body is like the lower and upper worlds.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:28: And now hear a wondrous piece of wisdom. Just as God is supreme and rules over man and over the whole world, above and below, so too is man, whenever he does the will of his Creator. For to Moses, peace be upon him, the Holy One, blessed be He, said concerning the incident of the calf (Deuteronomy 9:14): "Let Me alone, that I may destroy them"; and in the incident of Korah, the earth swallowed them and all that belonged to them at his word (Numbers 16). And Elijah, remembered for good, swore that there would be no dew or rain except by his word (1 Kings 17:1), and he brought down fire (1 Kings 18, and 2 Kings 1), and he killed the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18:9), and he revived the dead (1 Kings 17), and he decreed that Elisha should have a double portion of his spirit (2 Kings 2).
Orchot Tzadikim 28:29: And so all the holy men who were on earth ruled above and below by the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, when they did His will. Therefore be careful to fulfill His teachings, His statutes, and His commandments, so that you may merit abundant good that is stored away. And just as God knows and understands past and future, so too does man, to whom God has given wisdom. And just as God provides and gives bread to all flesh, so too does man sustain the members of his household, his servant, and his beast. And just as God repays good and evil, so too does man. And just as God builds the structure of the world, and the foundations of the earth, and the stretching out of the heavens, and the gathering-place of the seas, so too is man made to build, to found, to roof, to gather waters, to sow, to make things grow, to plant, and to do every kind of work; but with toil and hardship, and all according to the will of the Creator.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:30: And just as no creature can see God, so no creature can see the neshamah. And just as God knows the future, so too does man, at the time when his ruach and his body rest from occupying themselves with the labor of their needs, and the spirit of life rests and is quiet from concerning itself with the needs of the body — then he sees in his dreams things to come, and sees the spirits of the dead, and places he has never seen, and people he has never seen, and great matters and images, things he cannot see while awake. And just as there is no creature in the world that knows the secrets of God, so there is no creature among men that knows the secrets of the thoughts of a man's heart, save God alone, as it is written (Psalms 94:11): "The Lord knows the thoughts of man."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:31: And in many respects man resembles God in a small measure. In proportion to the small strength and the shortness of life that God has given him — the Holy One, blessed be He, added the evil inclination for his benefit and for his harm: in order to test him and try him between good and evil, and in order to adorn himself, to build and to plant, and to demolish and to uproot what is planted, and to kill and to chastise, to amass wealth, to wage war, to rule, and to plunder, and to rage exceedingly. And were it not for the evil inclination, out of dread of death he would not engage in procreation, nor would he build any building, nor would he desire to acquire property and possessions, nor would he plant, nor would he sow, for he would say in his heart: "Since the decree of death has been sealed, why should I labor for another?" And the whole world would be lost and destroyed.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:32: And the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create the world from the days of creation except that it be built up and conducted, through His abundant mercy, by the hand of man. And if a person prevails through his good inclination to subdue the evil inclination so that he does not sin before his Maker — for he uses his evil inclination to do everything in the fear of the blessed Name, without iniquity or transgression — this is his good fortune; happy is he, and happy is she who bore him.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:33: And just as man resembles God in a small measure, so too is the structure of his body like the whole world: He made him a skull for the head, like the firmament of the heavens above this firmament. He made him the upper roof of the mouth, in which are planted teeth and jaws, in the likeness of this firmament above us. And just as this firmament above us separates between the upper waters and the lower waters, so too the upper roof of the mouth separates between the moisture of the mouth and the moisture in the head and the moisture in the upper membrane. And just as God made His holy Presence dwell in the upper heavens which roof over the waters, as it is written (Psalms 104:3): "Who lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters" — so He made the spirit of the soul of life, and knowledge and understanding, dwell in the membrane of the brain of the head, which is spread over the brain and over the moisture. And see and understand the truth, that if the membrane of the brain is torn or punctured, a person dies at once, since it is there that the spirit of life dwells.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:34: And just as God, blessed be He, made His holy Presence dwell in the west, so too He made the brain dwell at the back of the head above the ears, and made the spirit of life dwell upon the brain. And just as the whole world endures and is conducted by the power of the one God, so the whole body is conducted by the power of the one spirit of life that God, blessed be He, gave it, and it endures thereby, remaining healthy and sustained until its end comes. And if any other, evil spirit becomes mixed into his body, it will not remain as it was at first.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:35: And just as He placed in the firmament of the heavens two great lights and five stars, so He created in man's head seven luminaries: two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, and the mouth. The right eye resembles the sun, and the left resembles Venus. The right nostril resembles Mercury, and the left resembles Mars. The mouth, the tongue, and the lips resemble Jupiter, the moon, and Saturn. And just as air was made between the firmament and the earth, so in the body of man the chest and the torso were made. And just as the wind returns within the air, in the void of the world, so the breath of the spirit of life goes out from the lung that is in the chest and the torso, which is the void of the body. And just as He spread the earth over the waters, so He stretched and spread the membrane of flesh that is over the liver, and over the stomach, and the intestines, and over the spleen — this is the flesh that lies between the lung and the liver and the spleen and the intestines and the stomach.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:36: And just as God, blessed be He, made birds and fish, and beasts and cattle — some innocent and merciful, not oppressing one another, and some cruel, preying upon and devouring one another — so too He made among men: the good were likened to the good birds and cattle, as it is said (Song of Songs 5:2): "My dove, my perfect one"; and it is said (Ezekiel 34:31): "And you, My flock, the flock of My pasture." And wicked men were likened to fierce beasts: to a lion, as it is written (Psalms 17:12): "He is like a lion that is greedy for prey"; and some are likened to bears and wolves, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:3): "Her judges are evening wolves."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:37: In the world there are trees and plants and fruits both good and bad. Some have a good scent and good fruits for healing and remedy, and there are plants and roots and fruits that bring death, like the herbs of deadly poison, and like thorns and thistles. The good were likened to the good, as it is written (Song of Songs 2:2-3): "Like a lily among thorns... like an apple tree among the trees of the forest." And the wicked were likened to the wicked, as it is written (2 Samuel 23:6): "But the worthless are all as thorns thrust away."
Orchot Tzadikim 28:38: And just as He made beneath the earth deeps, mud, and mire, so He made in man the upper cavity and the intestines, which receive food and drink. And just as creeping things and crawling things of every kind swarm from the mire and the mud, so in the intestines of man there swarm, from the sediment-mire of food and drink, creeping and crawling worms, long and short, large and small. And just as He made a gathering-place of waters in the world, so He made a gathering-place for the water of the feet — that is, the bladder, which is the urinary receptacle.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:39: And just as He made the foundations of the earth beneath it, so He made, as the foundation of the whole structure of the body, the hip bones on either side and the two thighs. And just as He made hollowed stones sunk in the deep, from between which the waters issue forth, so He made the two kidneys, from between which, through their own vessels, the water of the feet — that is, the urine — issues forth and passes to the bladder. And the moisture of the seed also passes and issues forth from between them to the testicles. And just as "deep calls unto deep," as it is written (Psalms 42:8): "Deep calls unto deep" — so the upper cavity, which is the stomach, calls to the intestines to receive from it the rest of the food and drink; and the intestines call to the vessels of the kidneys, which are like conduits, to receive the waters from them. The water of the feet is that which is filtered and separated from the food in the intestines, to go to the bladder. And the ducts of the kidneys call to the vessel of the bladder to receive that water from them, to carry it to be gathered within the bladder, which is like the lowest place, lower than all the deeps. And that same intestine calls also to the intestine of the stomach, to receive the waste and the excrement.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:40: And just as God made rivers to water the world, so He made in the body of man the veins, which are the blood vessels that draw the blood to water the whole body. And just as there are in the world clear and murky waters, sweet and salty and bitter — so it is with man: from his eyes come salty waters, from his nostrils come cold waters, and from his throat hot waters, and from his mouth sweet waters, and from his ears bitter waters, and the waters of urine are bitter and foul.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:41: In the world there are cold and hot winds; so too in man: when he opens his mouth and breathes out, the breath is hot, and when he closes his mouth and breathes out, the breath is cold. Thunder in the world is like the voice in man; lightning in the world is like a man's face shining like lightning. There are constellations in the world, and those who read the stars know the future from them — so too there are signs in man: when a person itches without a rash, without lice, and without a flea, those learned in this wisdom know the future from it; and likewise from the lines of a man's hand and the features of his face they know the future. This wisdom was held by the ancient sages, but it has been forgotten by later generations. And the sages are also able to know the future from trees and plants, and this is what was said of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, that he knew the speech of palm trees (Sukkah 28a) — meaning, he was expert in observing the movement of palm trees, and from this he knew the future.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:42: And just as, from the direction of the south — which is the right side of the world — come forth heat and blessed dews and blessed rains, so from the right side of a man comes forth the heat from the bile that hangs from the liver, and so too the moisture of the blood goes out from the liver, which is on the right side of man. And just as evil comes forth into the world from the north side of the world, so cold comes forth from the left side of man, from the spleen and from the black bile that dwells within the spleen. And just as evil comes forth into the world from the north, so every severe and grievous illness comes forth from the black bile that dwells in the spleen on the left side. And just as on the north side of the world is the dwelling place of all harmful spirits, and sparks, and terrors, and winds, and lightnings, and thunders, so it is the source of the black bile in the spleen on the left side, from which come the offspring of every severe and grievous illness, such as consumption, quartan fever, every kind of madness, fright, and trembling of the limbs.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:43: And just as vapors, which are like smoke, rise from the earth, and raise up the waters from the deeps into the air of the firmament to rain upon the earth, so smoke rises from the upper cavity and raises moisture up to the mouth and to the head; and from that moisture which rises from the innards flow the tears, the mucus of the nostrils, and the saliva of the mouth. And just as He created mountains in the world, so He created in the body of man the shoulders, the joints of the arms, the knee-joints upon the knees, the joints of the ankles, and the rest of the joints of all the limbs. And just as He created in the world stones and strong, hard rocks, so He created in man the teeth and the jaws, which are harder than iron and than any bone. And just as He created in the world hard and soft trees, so He created in man hard and soft bones. And just as He created in the world thick and hard earth, and moist and soft earth, so He created in man flesh corresponding to the soft earth, and skin corresponding to the hard earth.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:44: And just as some trees and plants bear fruit and seed, and some do not bear fruit and seed, so among men some beget children and some do not beget. And just as He causes plants to grow from the earth, so He causes the hair of the head and the beard to grow in man. And just as beasts and creeping things swarm in the forest and on the earth, so they swarm on a man's head and in his hair. And just as God created in the world the celestial axis, and stretched it across the firmament from east to west, from end to end, and the stars and constellations and everything in the world are attached to it, so He created in the body of man the white marrow within the vertebrae of the spine, and it stretches from the end of the brain of the head to the tailbone, and the twelve segments and the ribs and all the limbs of the body are attached to it on this side and that. And just as there are 365 days in the year, so there are 365 vessels in man.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:45: In sum: the Account of Creation and the Account of the Chariot are all hinted at within man in small measure, and one who knows the secret of this matter will understand the wonders of the exalted Name. Therefore man is called a "small world." And because the body of man is fashioned in the pattern of the upper world and the lower world, therefore the nefesh, which resembles its Creator in small measure, was placed within it.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:46: And therefore David said (Psalms 103:1): "Bless the Lord, O my soul." And why did he tell the soul to bless? David said (Vayikra Rabbah 4:8): This soul fills the whole body and outlasts the body, yet does not eat, and it bears the body. And it is alone within the body, and it is pure, and it sees but is not seen, and it does not sleep. So too the Holy One, blessed be He, fills His world and outlasts everything, as it is said (Psalms 102:27): "They shall perish, but You shall endure." And the Holy One, blessed be He, does not sleep, as it is said (Psalms 121:4): "Behold, He neither slumbers nor sleeps." And He is alone and pure. And He sees everything, and nothing else sees Him. Therefore let the soul, which possesses all these qualities, come and praise the Holy One, blessed be He, who possesses all these qualities.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:47: The nefesh sits and considers who created it, and then it puts on humility and the fear of the Name. Therefore a person must look at himself and understand his own condition: from where his root and stock came, and how he was formed from a filthy drop of seed, and afterward became a lump of flesh, and had breathed into him a spirit from on high, and was woven together with bones and sinews, blood and marrow, and clothed with skin and flesh. And he was shaped with the features of a face and the stature of a countenance. And how his nostrils were bored through to his throat, to breathe and to smell, and his ears to hear, and the openings of his eyes to see. And within the eye there are several colors, and eyelashes, and a mouth and throat, and palate and tongue, and lips to open and close, and jaws and cheeks, and joints of hands and feet, and the cavity of the body, and fingers and their joints and their nails.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:48: And let him understand how each person differs from his fellow, and how he was confined nine months in his mother's womb, and came out naked, blind, deaf, and lame. Let him consider all this and say in his heart: Who opened your mouth, your eyes, and your ears? And who made for you all the arrangements of your body? And in the days of your youth, who darkened your hair — for if one were to wash the hair with every soap and cleanser in the world, it would not avail to whiten even a single hair — yet in the days of your old age it whitens by itself? On such matters as these you should reflect always, and you will become humble and lowly of spirit and God-fearing.
Orchot Tzadikim 28:49: "The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man" (Ecclesiastes 12:13).
Orchot Tzadikim 28:50: Finished and complete; praise to God, Creator of the world.
